page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory performance, with large-block write bandwidth reaching top-tier levels at 195.06 GB/sec and a top-tier PassMark memory score. Single-threaded decompression and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also rank in the top tier. Compute performance is robust, with PassMark CPU scores and extended instruction tests placing in the top 25%. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores reside in the average tier, indicating steady parallel processing capabilities. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds on small and medium language models, alongside strong static web serving throughput of 80.02 GB/sec.

Given its balanced resource allocation and dedicated CPU model, this server offers high resource density and reliable compute performance without the risk of noisy-neighbor interference. The minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external block storage for data-heavy applications. Consequently, the instance is well-suited for memory-intensive text processing, web serving, lightweight LLM inference, and general-purpose enterprise workloads that do not rely on large local disk storage.
description: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is a general-purpose server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family, featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 32 dedicated vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 128.0 GB of RAM. Operating at 2.0 GHz, the CPU supports AVX-512 and cryptographic instructions, backed by a 32 MB L3 cache. While local storage is limited to a 1 GB NVMe SSD, the instance delivers top-tier memory write bandwidth of 195.06 GB/sec and strong PassMark CPU performance. Benchmarks highlight exceptional single-threaded compression and text processing capabilities, alongside efficient text generation for small and medium language models. This hardware profile makes the server highly effective for static web serving, text processing, and general-purpose workloads requiring dedicated compute resources and high memory capacity, provided external storage is utilized.
